headline: Ramaphosa Fights His Own Impeachment Evidence Leader
script: Ramaphosa's impeachment process just hit a fresh obstacle. Two weeks ago, Parliament's impeachment committee voted 9 to 7 to recommend advocate Thandazani Madonsela as chief evidence leader for the Phala Phala inquiry into the president, with the ANC abstaining. Now, in a letter sent Tuesday night, Ramaphosa is formally objecting, arguing Madonsela has a conflict of interest: the president removed him from the Judicial Service Commission back in 2022, and Madonsela recently gave the ANC legal advice tied to this very impeachment. Opposition MPs aren't buying it. EFF leader Julius Malema said bluntly: 'He is not going to choose his own judge.' The committee has now paused to seek its own legal opinion. Why it matters: this is the process meant to hold South Africa's president accountable over stolen dollars in a game farm couch, and every procedural fight like this pushes real accountability further down the road.
why_it_matters: It's a live test of whether SA's most powerful office can be held accountable through Parliament, shaping young voters' trust in institutions ahead of the November local elections.
